skills.trigger: When evaluating serial chest radiographs to distinguish Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP) from other causes of pulmonary consolidation based on temporal evolution.
steps: Identify the location and extent of airspace opacities (consolidation) in the initial imaging study.
Compare with follow-up imaging to assess for resolution of the original opacity and simultaneous appearance of new consolidation in a different anatomical region.

Recognize this specific pattern of 'migratory pulmonary infiltrates' (clearing in one area while appearing in another) as a hallmark feature supporting a diagnosis of COP, distinguishing it from static pneumonia or progressive fibrotic disease.
